reviews.comment: Very little time between topics to ask questions. The slides were too dense with math notation, and I retained little from lecture. I recommend the MATH 323 help sessions and his office hours. Work on the practice problems he emails. Three quarters of the class skipped after Exam 1. Median final grade was 91%.

Lecture were on the bland side but the slides are decent. Homeworks (have extra credit) are very hard and time consuming (could spend more than an hour on a problem and still be half way done).  Exams were on the harder side but you will score fine if you do all the problems on his practice exam. Helpful during office hours.
a surprisingly lenient and good professor for one of the hardest math classes, he gave a lot of extra credit on hws and graded tests really leniently so I love my king 😁😁

His slides are really, really good, his lectures are pretty good as well. Homeworks can be challenging but other sections probably had harder homeworks and every homework has a substantial amount of extra credit. His exams were really easy, probably too easy. Overall a very interesting class and not too stressful either.

i was terribly depressed for reasons unrelated to the course the entire semester, but the way the class was structured was very accommodating. there is a lot of homework that is time consuming but he gives a lot of bonus points on both the homework and exams. the exams are very doable if you have done the review. you learn a lot in this course!

You'll be fine if you remember everything in calc 1 and 2.  Lectures are not the greatest, but the slides are good. The weekly homework is hard, usually requires some proof technique in the slides. Exams are super easy compared to the homework, and he is very generous with grading the exams, as long as your proof idea is fine and did the review.
Homeworks are long and take a lot of time. Lectures just read out what is on the slides, but equations and problems are never worked out in real time.

Lectures are honestly not amazing, but they get the info across that you need. Exams are extremely straight forward with a given bank of problems, just study them and you will be totally fine. Even if you mess up he gives very very generous partial credit. HW can be tough but nothing too bad. Lectures aren't required but showing up can be helpful.

Makes linear algebra understandable but he goes on tangents sometimes abt math proofs and it's difficult to follow along once the concepts get more advanced. The test bank is given as practice for the test so tests are mostly easy (one bonus question worth 15 pts on each test).

Yes, his lectures are boring but all of the content is clearly written out in slides and can be easily used on the homework. He also gives EASY EXAMS!! All questions on the exam will be given a week in advance on the "study guide" with example problems

I really enjoyed Dr. Vorobets' class and the material he taught. Textbook is easy to understand and informative but not necessarily required. He uploads all his lecture/review slides and has helpful review sessions before exams. Weekly quizzes but attendance not mandatory and no homework. Dry at times but very kind and makes jokes occasionally.

He is a very caring professor.His slides are short and to the point.They're available online as well. He does reviews before every exam that are pretty close to what will be on the exam.There were bonus problems on every exam that were fair and close to the other problems on the exam where the midterms had 115 points, 130 for the final out of 100.

He is lenient on grading. Also, for each test, he gives you practice problems (e.g., 5 sections with 20 questions each so 100 problems total) and he picks one of those from each test. So, do those and u already did the "test". He is really nice and understanding. Please take him if you get a chance. Homework was weekly, but due 11:59 pm on Fridays.

If you are taking M323 or M304, Professor Vorobets is the best option. He provides clear expectations and clear grading feedback on assignments. He also provides 100 practice problems and a review. The practice problems are very similar to some of the exam questions, so it is very helpful to know how to work the problems. Would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Nice guy who knows his stuff, but I took nothing away from this class. I've never fallen asleep in a lecture before, but this class certainly did.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I greatly appreciate the powerpoints he makes and how informative they are. But for someone who is a visual learner, it was a challenging class. While his powerpoints show problems and solutions, there is no working out the problems, only him verbally explaining the steps. Which, for me, felt very confusing and overwhelming. Nice guy though.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Vorobets was quite a dry lecturer and I really did not understand much from this class. However, he grades fairly liberally, so as long as you're trying your best you won't be punished for not understanding everything completely. Difficult class, but a good enough instructor to get through it with minimal trouble.

Not bad overall. Although no notes on board, everything is clear on his slides. The weekly homework may be kinds of time consuming, but you can find the needed definitions and theorems in the slides. Besides, this course is a helpful preparation for graduate level abstract algebra.

Easiest professor ever. He posts a question bank before each test, and then assigns you a problem for each section on the test, so as long as you do at least 1 of the problems from each section, it's an easy A. His lectures can be super boring, but he is a really nice guy outside of class. Definitely take for 311.

This class was was for sure one of the most in depth math class I have ever taken. But Professor Vorobets gives you all possible exams questions the night before the test, and then chooses some for the exam day which makes things easier. Also, the only time I emailed him he was really nice and allowed me to submit my work late and still count it.

This is by far the hardest class I have ever taken. Had it not been for COVID making my class switch to online and Vorobets making things easier as a result, and the 409 tutor (Sheagan John), I would have failed. The lectures don't help, so it's pretty much all on you to learn everything. I would highly recommend going to the tutoring sessions.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself for Advanced Calculus, it's hard because of the proof based. Other than that, it gets a little easier. As a prof, he just lectures from the slides without writing on the board. Thankfully he grades very fairly which is technically a curve and his sample tests are nearly identical to actual exams but the format is the same.

Dr. Vorobets definitely gives a pretty dry lecture but for only teaching from a power point does a pretty good job. His sample test are very similar to the actual test. There is absolutely no curve but is the most generous grader I have ever come across. Definitely a great pick for 311 would definitely take again.

Power point lectures. There are theorems, proofs, and examples in his power points. He puts them on his website along with his reviews which very accurately reflect his tests. I would like to emphasize what someone else said about his humor. He is typically not too energetic, but he is actually really funny sometimes.

Summarized into a few points: - Exams were similar to his review and sample exam - Weekly homework was straightforward and was an easy 100% - Lectures are via PPT which is made available so attendance is not mandatory - You can easily make an A if you do the homework and review problems.

It should be made evident that the lectures are given via ppt, and there are almost no examples in the ppts throughout the semester; you are just given a plethora of theorems with no application (ironically it is called applied mathematics). Anything I learned was from past professors and Khan Academy (thanks Sal). There were no TAs for this class.
At first, Dr. Vorobets doesn't seem energetic nor enthusiastic, but he knows how to crack a good joke at the right time. Grading is very generous, and the exams are very similar to the sample tests.

His lectures are really boring. He doesn't have enough visual aids. He's really nice. His reviews are really helpful, and his exams end up being similar to his exams. Exams are not too hard, but there's only 4 questions. Gives partial credit. Really polite in his emails. Not too hard of a class.

Yaroslav is the best math prof I've had so far at A&M, I enjoyed his lectures and thought he was a pretty funny guy. It's important to note that he can't write on the board, he uses powerpoints that can be pretty hard to follow at times, but he's a really great lecturer if you pay attention. Study the reviews for the exam and you'll finish with >B

Dr. Vorobets was a pretty average lecturer. He never felt particularly enthusiastic nor engaging, pretty much read from what he prepared and took questions if they were asked. His notes were pretty good however and his tests weren't too bad. He offered tons of practice through his weekly optional homeworks. Do them though, extremely important.

Dr. Vorobets assigns optional weekly homework. If you learn how to do the 10 problems, the quiz is simple. He offers bonus questions on tests, so go through his website to find old quiz problems for some extra practice. Gives full review before each exam, and if you know how to do those, you'll do just fine in the class.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT
